note: Per-variant results. Phases 4-5 (integrated forward/backward fidelity) were NOT executed: no variant cleared the evaluator performance floor (median S_eval >= 4.0), and the HARD DROP trigger fired (median S_eval < 2.5 for all variants in both primary scenes). Numerical reference validation (phase 1) IS available and confirms the reconstruction is correct, so the negative result is a performance one, not a numerical one.

gates.hard_drop: any primary scene median S_eval < 2.5  OR  all NUMERIC_PASS S_FB < 1.30  OR  no variant passes numerical gate

DIRECT.note: 1 MUFU.EX2 per pixel (SASS); the SFU exp is the inner-loop critical path

sass_static_inspection.interpretation: DIRECT is SFU-exp-bound: exactly one dynamic MUFU.EX2 (exp2) per pixel, 84 SASS lines. QSCAN's 4 MUFU.EX2 are the LEADER seed exps (G0, r0, k, k^pos) — one set per subgroup — that EVERY lane depends on, so they remain on the critical path (they cannot be overlapped away because the lane's G_j = G0 * prefix_j needs G0 first). The prefix scan adds SHFL + FMUL (~192 extra SASS lines). The per-lane quadratic FMA (the only work QSCAN would reduce) is only ~3 FFMAs — a negligible fraction of the exp's SFU latency. Hence QSCAN ~ DIRECT on an A100 with a wide MUFU pipeline.

real_trace_characterization.note: Captured from the frozen C0 forward raster (TILE_SIZE=16), 32 x-positions per visible (gaussian, image-row), stratified by live-lane population (alpha>=1/255 cull).
real_trace_characterization.interpretation: Live-lane populations are near-zero: the C0 Gaussians are tight (MAX_EXTEND=3.33 sigma culling), so an on-tile (gaussian, row) has ~0-2 live pixels out of 32. The alpha-cull is already extremely sparse. This means (a) the inner loop is mostly exp-evaluations that are about to be culled anyway, and (b) there is little redundant per-pixel work for a quotient reconstruction to eliminate. The exp remains the per-pixel op.

decision.reason: median S_eval < 2.5 for EVERY variant in BOTH primary scenes (room AND bicycle). Best variant QSCAN8 median S_eval ~0.97 << 2.5.
